name: Moulin-à-Vent

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

terms: France's protected place names. A wine sold under one must follow that appellation's rules. The EU's term for the same tier is PDO, or AOP in French.
There is no legal or agreed definition of old, so the words promise nothing on their own.
The middle tier, from 38 villages in the north of the region, with the crus, such as Fleurie, above it.

notes: Moulin-à-Vent makes the fullest bodied and most powerful Beaujolais.
Some producers age it in oak, giving more tannin and structure than other Beaujolais.
It can keep developing in bottle for up to 10 years, gaining Burgundian structure and complexity.

blurb.text: A Beaujolais cru for red wine from Gamay, on the border of the Rhône and Saône-et-Loire departments, in parts of Chénas and Romanèche-Thorins. Its name means windmill, and it gained AOC status in 1936.
